sections.overview: The graceful shark is an Indo-West Pacific requiem shark of coastal and continental-shelf waters, recorded from the Gulf region to northern Australia.
sections.identification: It is a medium-sized streamlined shark; Australian records give a maximum of 167 cm total length, while reliable records can be confused with similar blacktip sharks.
sections.habitat: It uses continental-shelf waters to at least 50 m and is especially associated with mangrove habitats in northern Australia.
sections.diet: Its diet includes fishes; species-specific prey data are limited, and fishing records often group it with other blacktip sharks.
sections.behavior: It is a mobile coastal predator, but detailed movement and lifespan information remains sparse.
sections.reproduction: It is a live-bearing shark; available Australian syntheses report maturity near 110 cm total length in both sexes, while other reproductive details remain poorly known.
sections.ecology: It can be mistaken for the blacktip shark C. limbatus or spinner shark C. brevipinna; it is distinct from the grey reef shark C. amblyrhynchos despite the similar scientific name.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports the current global IUCN category as Vulnerable; fishing pressure and identification problems complicate estimates of population trends.
